extracted.intended_audience: PR professionals (agency and in-house PR teams) seeking KPIs and measurement guidance
extracted.subtask_description: A practical guide to which Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) public relations teams should track, why some common metrics are misleading, and how to interpret media, social, website/SEO, advertising, and crisis-related metrics to prove PR impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising Value Equivalent (AVE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Attempts to compare a PR mention’s space with paid advertising space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outdated metric: tells you nothing about the quality, impact or credibility of earned media and doesn’t show if you reached your target audience or delivered key messages. Can misleadingly increase during a PR crisis. If stakeholders insist, tools (like Prowly) can still track AVE alongside more meaningful metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain reach (UVPM / UVM)
rubrics_metrics.description: UVPM (Unique Visitors per Month) measures the potential size of the audience that could have been reached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Problematic because the 'month' timeframe is too broad for fast news cycles and it doesn't indicate whether mentions impact your target group. Treat cautiously or supplement with more targeted metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mention estimated reach
rubrics_metrics.description: An estimate of the number of people who could have seen a particular article within the past month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be helpful for planning and assessing popular outlets, but not meaningful alone for understanding impact on your target audience or the value of a specific publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earned Media Value (EMV)
rubrics_metrics.description: A metric similar to AVE that assigns a monetary value to earned mentions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essentially the same problems as AVE: does not reflect quality, credibility, or real impact; use with caution and alongside outcome-focused metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media tiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Grouping publishers into tiers (Tier 1, Tier 2, etc.) based on relative value to your target audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track number of mentions in each tier to gauge reach with key demographics. Example: pick top 5 Tier 1 articles each week and assess quality with a checklist/scoring system. Use tags to categorize mentions for reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top mentions
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and track your most impactful media coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generate lists of top mentions by industry category and sort by sentiment, domain authority, article reach, backlinks, date published, etc. Example: choose top 10 mentions per query and display on a dashboard to show which coverage drives best results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience analytics (outlet/platform engagement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand which outlets and platforms your target audience engages with most.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to build a 'true media list' (not just emails): identify outlets relevant to the client's industry and audience, pick top media choices for special attention, and set filters to find outlets matching the customer profile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Total amount of press coverage an organization or campaign receives, including articles, news segments, and interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure to show overall visibility; combine with quality/sentiment measures to assess value of coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall media presence
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive measurement of the entirety of your media coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essentially synonymous with media coverage; useful to present an aggregate view of brand visibility within the media landscape.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media mentions
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of times your brand is mentioned in the media and online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps demonstrate media interest, extent of coverage, and can be paired with sentiment to evaluate the tone of coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential reach
rubrics_metrics.description: An estimate of how many people could see your content based on circulation, viewership, and followership of outlets that covered your story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considered a vanity metric; advisable to use alongside more meaningful, outcome-focused metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Total number of times your content is viewed across the media landscape.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives scale but not depth of impact; best reported with conversion or engagement metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media engagements
rubrics_metrics.description: Audience involvement metrics on social platforms (likes, shares, comments, retweets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tracks interest and interaction; use to gauge resonance of messages and to feed into broader PR reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentiment analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification of the context and tone of media coverage and social mentions as positive, negative, or neutral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides insight into public perception and brand attitudes. AI-assisted monitoring can extract sentiment at scale. Particularly important during crises, when sentiment KPIs are stressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Website traffic
rubrics_metrics.description: Total number of visitors to a website, with breakdown by source (organic, direct, referral, social).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure PR impact on site visits using unique visitors, unique pageviews, bounce rate, and referrals from target media; integrate Google Analytics/CRM data for attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earned traffic
rubrics_metrics.description: Traffic you haven't paid for (organic search, social mentions, backlinks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track backlinks and earned traffic to attribute web visits to PR efforts; PR tools can count and display earned traffic automatically to credit PR activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain Authority
rubrics_metrics.description: A search-engine-ranking score (Semrush-based in this guide) predicting how well a website will rank, usually on a 0–100 scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher scores indicate stronger authority; use as a proxy for outlet quality when assessing mentions and backlinks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Backlinks
rubrics_metrics.description: External links from other websites that point to your content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track the number and quality of backlinks over a campaign to attribute SEO and traffic benefits to PR. Tools can show where your website is linked and provide associated metrics (domain reach, domain authority, article reach).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversions
rubrics_metrics.description: Desired end actions from audience (purchases, sign-ups, leads, app downloads).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The business outcomes PR can influence; use CRM and analytics to trace conversions back to PR sources where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion rate
rubrics_metrics.description: The percentage of viewers who completed a desired action (converted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to assess effectiveness of PR-driven traffic in producing bottom-line results.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPC (Cost Per Click)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amount paid for each click in paid campaigns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common marketing metric used to measure cost-efficiency of paid efforts; relevant when PR teams handle paid activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA (Cost Per Acquisition)
rubrics_metrics.description: How much it costs to acquire a new customer or lead (total campaign cost divided by acquisitions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for teams combining PR and marketing to assess financial efficiency of campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: CTR (Click Through Rate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage of viewers who click on a specific element (ad, link, button).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates direct effectiveness of messaging and creative in driving engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROAS (Return on Advertising Spend)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compares financial outcomes of a campaign with its costs to measure profitability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: More marketing-focused but relevant for teams integrating PR and paid strategies to evaluate campaign profitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share of Voice (SoV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compares your brand's presence in industry conversations to that of top competitors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure how your brand performs against competition across online content and industry conversations; useful for benchmarking visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of Coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of coverage based on level of detail, sentiment, and impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality coverage is typically in-depth, positive, and published in reputable outlets; pair quality scoring with quantity metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographical presence
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution of media coverage across different regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyzes where a brand has greatest influence and visibility; useful for geo-targeted campaigns and regional PR evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key message penetration
rubrics_metrics.description: How effectively your core messages are communicated across media coverage and social mentions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure to ensure communication goals are met; can be tracked via keyword/message occurrence and qualitative content analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis communications effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of how efficiently strategies mitigate negative publicity and protect brand reputation during a crisis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track timing and accuracy of information communicated, changes in sentiment and coverage, and whether reputation was protected or restored; use crisis examples to benchmark performance.
